title: Paella
subtitle: Spanish saffron rice with chicken, chorizo, and seafood
excerpt: Short-grain rice cooked with saffron stock, chicken, chorizo, prawns, and mussels until a golden crust forms on the base. Spain's most famous dish, cooked in a single wide pan.

recipe.sourceNotes: Paella originates from the Valencia region of Spain, where the original version was made with rabbit, snails, green beans, and flat butter beans. The seafood version now most familiar internationally is a later adaptation. The name refers to the wide, flat pan in which the dish is cooked, not to the rice or the flavourings. The defining characteristic of a properly made paella is the socarrat: the caramelised, slightly crisp crust of rice that forms on the base of the pan in the final minutes of cooking. This requires controlling the heat carefully and not stirring the rice once the stock is added. Saffron is non-negotiable: it provides both the characteristic golden colour and a flavour that nothing else replicates.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, shallow paella pan or large frying pan.

content.text: The rice must never be stirred once the stock goes in. Stirring releases starch and makes the rice creamy and sticky, like a risotto, which is not the correct texture for paella. The rice should absorb the stock and then, in the last 2 to 3 minutes, form the socarrat on the base. Listen for a gentle crackling and smell carefully: it should smell toasted but not burnt. Remove from the heat and rest under foil for 5 minutes before serving.

items.preparation: paella rice or Spanish bomba rice

content.text: Heat the oil in a wide paella pan over high heat. Season the chicken and fry skin-side down for 5 minutes until golden. Turn and cook for 3 minutes. Remove and set aside. Fry the chorizo for 2 minutes. Remove and set aside.

Reduce to medium heat. Fry the onion and red pepper for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, paprika, and saffron water. Cook for 3 minutes until slightly reduced.

Add the rice and stir to coat for 1 minute. Pour in the hot stock. Arrange the chicken pieces and chorizo in the rice. Bring to a vigorous boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Do not stir. Cook for 15 minutes.

Nestle the prawns and mussels into the rice. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the prawns are pink and the mussels have opened. Discard any mussels that have not opened. Increase the heat for the final 2 minutes to develop the socarrat. Remove from the heat, cover with foil, and rest for 5 minutes. Scatter with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
